questions.question: In an angiospermous embryo sac, what is the ploidy level of the functional megaspore, central cell (after vegetative triple fusion), and zygote respectively?

questions.subtopic: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants (Filiform Apparatus)
questions.question: In the mature female gametophyte of an angiosperm, what is the specialized structure and essential function of the filiform apparatus located in the synergids?
options: Finger-like cellular thickenings at the micropylar tip that guide the entry of the pollen tube into the synergid
Chalazal extensions that store starch reserves for early embryo nourishment
Hardened outer cuticular spines that physically block polyspermy
Membranous partitions that divide the central cell into antipodal compartments
questions.explanation: The synergids have special cellular thickenings at the micropylar tip called filiform apparatus. The filiform apparatus plays an indispensable guiding role in directing the pollen tube into the cytoplasm of one of the synergids during pollen-pistil interaction.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 12 Biology Board Paper 2024 / NCERT Chapter 1 Section 1.2.2

questions.subtopic: Principles of Inheritance (Down's vs Turner's Syndrome)
questions.question: What are the respective chromosomal karyotypes and clinical diagnostic features of Down's syndrome and Turner's syndrome in humans?
options: Down's syndrome is Trisomy 21 (47, +21) showing furrowed tongue and broad palm; Turner's syndrome is monosomy of X (45, X0) in females showing sterile rudimentary ovaries and short stature
Down's syndrome is 47, XXY showing gynecomastia; Turner's syndrome is 47, XYY showing tall aggressive males
Down's syndrome is deletion of chromosome 5p; Turner's syndrome is trisomy of chromosome 18
Down's syndrome is 45, X0; Turner's syndrome is 47, +21
questions.explanation: Down's syndrome is caused by the presence of an additional copy of chromosome 21 (trisomy 21, total 47 chromosomes). The affected individual is short statured with small round head, furrowed tongue and partially open mouth, and broad palm with characteristic palm crease. Turner's syndrome is caused by the absence of one of the X chromosomes (monosomy 45, X0). Such females are sterile as ovaries are rudimentary, along with short stature and lack of secondary sexual characteristics.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 12 Biology Board Paper 2024 / NCERT Chapter 4 Section 4.4.3

questions.subtopic: Molecular Basis of Inheritance (Transcription Unit Organization)
questions.question: In a transcription unit of double-stranded DNA, what defines the template strand and in which direction does DNA-dependent RNA polymerase synthesize mRNA?
options: The strand with 3' -> 5' polarity serves as the template strand; RNA polymerase synthesizes RNA exclusively in the 5' -> 3' direction
The strand with 5' -> 3' polarity serves as the template strand; RNA polymerase synthesizes RNA in the 3' -> 5' direction
Both strands serve simultaneously as templates in opposite directions
The coding strand with 5' -> 3' polarity is directly transcribed into transfer RNA
questions.explanation: Since the DNA-dependent RNA polymerase catalyzes polymerization in only one direction, that is, 5' -> 3', the strand that has polarity 3' -> 5' acts as a template and is referred to as the template strand. The other strand with polarity 5' -> 3' (and sequence identical to RNA except thymine instead of uracil) is displaced and referred to as the coding strand.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 12 Biology Board Paper 2024 / NCERT Chapter 5 Section 5.3.1

questions.question: What is the critical functional advantage of a sparged stirred-tank bioreactor over a simple stirred-tank bioreactor in high-density bacterial cultures?
options: Sterile air bubbles are sparged throughout the vessel, dramatically multiplying the surface area for gas-liquid oxygen mass transfer
It eliminates the need for foam control or mechanical cooling jackets
It permits purely anaerobic fermentation without dissolved oxygen
It uses centrifugal gravity to eliminate cellular waste continuously
questions.explanation: In a sparged stirred-tank bioreactor, sterile air is sparged (injected as fine bubbles) through the culture medium. The vast number of small rising bubbles dramatically increases the gas-liquid surface area across which oxygen can dissolve, ensuring high dissolved oxygen availability for rapidly respiring aerobic microbial biomass.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 12 Biology Board Paper 2024 / NCERT Chapter 9 Section 9.3

questions.question: According to Allen's Rule in ecological physiology, mammals from colder climates generally possess:
options: Shorter ears and shorter limbs to minimize heat loss through body surface area
Longer extremities and thinner fur to dissipate excess metabolic heat
Lighter body pigmentation and absence of subcutaneous fat layers
Enlarged peripheral capillary beds that radiate heat into the environment
questions.explanation: Allen's Rule states that mammals from colder climates generally have shorter ears and limbs to minimize surface area-to-volume ratio and reduce heat loss. In polar seas, aquatic mammals like seals also possess a thick layer of fat (blubber) beneath their skin that acts as an insulator and reduces the loss of body heat.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 12 Biology Board Paper 2024 / NCERT Chapter 11 Section 11.1.3

questions.subtopic: Human Health and Disease (Opioids vs Cannabinoids)
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches the drug class with its botanical source and physiological receptor site?
options: Opioids (Heroin/Morphine) — Extracted from latex of Papaver somniferum; bind to specific opioid receptors in the central nervous system and gastrointestinal tract
Cannabinoids — Extracted from Erythroxylum coca; bind to dopamine transport channels
Cocaine — Extracted from Cannabis sativa; binds to acetylcholine receptors at neuromuscular junctions
Morphine — Extracted from Atropa belladonna; acts as a hallucinogen on cardiac muscarinic receptors
questions.explanation: Opioids are drugs that bind to specific opioid receptors present in our central nervous system and gastrointestinal tract. Heroin (diacetylmorphine) is a white, odourless, bitter crystalline compound obtained by acetylation of morphine, which is extracted from the latex of poppy plant Papaver somniferum. Heroin is a depressant and slows down body functions.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 12 Biology Board Paper 2024 / NCERT Chapter 7 Section 7.6

questions.subtopic: Molecular Basis of Inheritance (DNA Replication Fork Discontinuity)
questions.question: During DNA replication in E. coli, why is DNA synthesis continuous on one template strand (leading strand) but discontinuous on the other (lagging strand)?
options: DNA-dependent DNA polymerase can catalyze polymerization only in the 5' -> 3' direction, requiring multiple RNA primers and Okazaki fragment synthesis on the 5' -> 3' template
Helicase unwinds the two parental DNA strands at unequal speeds
Single-strand DNA-binding proteins degrade the 3'-hydroxyl terminus on the lagging strand
DNA ligase inhibits RNA primer extension on the leading template strand
questions.explanation: DNA-dependent DNA polymerase catalyzes polymerization in only one direction, that is, 5' -> 3'. Consequently, on one strand (the template with polarity 3' -> 5'), the replication is continuous (leading strand), while on the other (the template with polarity 5' -> 3'), it is discontinuous as short Okazaki fragments (lagging strand). These fragments are subsequently joined by the enzyme DNA ligase.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 12 Biology Board Paper 2024 / NCERT Chapter 5 Section 5.4.1

questions.question: In a phenotypic frequency distribution graph, what type of natural selection occurs when individuals at both peripheral extremes of the distribution are favored over intermediate phenotypes, resulting in two distinct peaks?
questions.explanation: Natural selection can lead to: (1) Stabilization (more individuals acquire mean character value); (2) Directional change (more individuals acquire value other than the mean character value, shifting the curve in one direction); or (3) Disruption (more individuals acquire peripheral character value at both ends of the distribution curve, forming two separate phenotypic peaks).
questions.citation: CBSE Class 12 Biology Board Paper 2024 / NCERT Chapter 6 Section 6.7

questions.question: Why is the infusion of genetically engineered lymphocytes containing functional ADA cDNA not a permanent cure for SCID in a patient with adenosine deaminase deficiency?
options: Because mature human lymphocytes are not immortal cells and have a finite lifespan, requiring periodic infusions
Because the retroviral vector triggers host humoral rejection against ADA within days
Because the introduced cDNA integrates exclusively into non-transcribed heterochromatin
Because ADA enzyme undergoes rapid enzymatic deamination by gastric proteases
questions.explanation: In clinical gene therapy for ADA deficiency, lymphocytes from the patient's blood are cultured and transformed with functional ADA cDNA using a retroviral vector. As these mature circulating lymphocytes are not immortal, the patient requires periodic infusion of such genetically engineered cells. A permanent cure is possible only if the gene isolated from marrow cells producing ADA is introduced into cells at early embryonic stages.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 12 Biology Board Paper 2024 / NCERT Chapter 10 Section 10.2.2

questions.question: What is the primary distinction between a Grazing Food Chain (GFC) and a Detritus Food Chain (DFC) regarding initial energy flow?
options: GFC begins with living autotrophic producers and is the major conduit of energy flow in aquatic ecosystems, whereas DFC begins with dead organic matter and accounts for the major energy flow in terrestrial forest ecosystems
GFC operates without decomposers, whereas DFC requires solar photosynthesis at every trophic level
GFC always has an inverted biomass pyramid, whereas DFC always has an inverted energy pyramid
GFC consists strictly of apex carnivores, whereas DFC is restricted to unicellular algae
questions.explanation: The grazing food chain (GFC) begins with living green plants (producers). In an aquatic ecosystem, GFC is the major conduit for energy flow. The detritus food chain (DFC) begins with dead organic matter and is made up of decomposers (heterotrophic fungi and bacteria). In a terrestrial ecosystem, a much larger fraction of energy flows through the detritus food chain than through the GFC.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 12 Biology Board Paper 2024 / NCERT Chapter 12 Section 12.3

questions.subtopic: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants (Chasmogamy vs Cleistogamy)
questions.question: What is an undeniable EVOLUTIONARY DISADVANTAGE of obligate cleistogamous flowers despite their assured seed production?
options: Continuous self-pollination over generations leads to inbreeding depression and lack of genetic variation
Complete dependence on nocturnal insect pollinators for seed dispersal
Production of non-viable polyploid seeds that cannot germinate in soil
Susceptibility to flower predation due to wide petal exposure
questions.explanation: While cleistogamy guarantees seed production even in the total absence of pollinators, its severe evolutionary disadvantage is that it enforces strict, continuous self-pollination (autogamy). This leads to lack of genetic recombination, zero new genetic variations, and eventual inbreeding depression.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 12 Biology Board Paper 2024 / NCERT Chapter 1 Section 1.2.3

questions.question: In Alexander von Humboldt's species-area equation: log S = log C + Z log A, what is the ecological significance of the regression coefficient (slope of the line, Z)?
options: Z-values generally range between 0.1 to 0.2 for small local regions, but steepen dramatically to 0.6 to 1.2 when analyzing very large areas like entire continents
Z-values are always constant at 2.0 regardless of taxonomic group or geographic scale
Z-values decrease towards zero as habitat area expands indefinitely
Z-values represent the total number of endemic plant species in tropical rain forests
questions.explanation: German naturalist Alexander von Humboldt observed that species richness increases with exploring area, but only up to a limit. On a log scale, the relationship is a straight line: log S = log C + Z log A. Ecologists have discovered that Z-values typically lie in the range of 0.1 to 0.2 regardless of taxonomic group or region. However, if species-area relationships are analyzed across very large areas like an entire continent, the slope is much steeper, with Z-values in the range of 0.6 to 1.2 (e.g. 1.15 for frugivorous birds and mammals in tropical forests).
questions.citation: CBSE Class 12 Biology Board Paper 2024 / NCERT Chapter 13 Section 13.1.2

questions.subtopic: Case Study 1: Principles of Inheritance (Dihybrid Test Cross)
questions.question: A dihybrid pea plant heterozygous for round yellow seeds (RrYy) is test-crossed with a double recessive wrinkled green parent (rryy). What phenotypic ratio is expected in the resulting progeny?
options: 1 Round Yellow : 1 Round Green : 1 Wrinkled Yellow : 1 Wrinkled Green (1 : 1 : 1 : 1)
9 Round Yellow : 3 Round Green : 3 Wrinkled Yellow : 1 Wrinkled Green (9 : 3 : 3 : 1)
1 Round Yellow : 2 Round Green : 1 Wrinkled Green (1 : 2 : 1)
questions.explanation: A test cross involves crossing an individual showing dominant traits with a homozygous recessive parent. The heterozygous parent RrYy produces 4 types of gametes in equal proportions (25% each): RY, Ry, rY, ry. The homozygous recessive parent rryy produces only one type of gamete: ry. Combining these yields four equal phenotypic classes: RrYy (Round Yellow), Rryy (Round Green), rrYy (Wrinkled Yellow), and rryy (Wrinkled Green) in a 1 : 1 : 1 : 1 ratio.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 12 Biology Board Paper 2024 / NCERT Chapter 4 Section 4.3

questions.subtopic: Case Study 2: Biotechnology Principles (PCR Thermal Steps)
questions.question: What is the correct thermal sequence and biochemical function of the three steps in each cycle of the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR)?
options: Denaturation (~94°C: melts dsDNA into single strands) -> Annealing (~54°C: oligonucleotide primers bind) -> Extension (~72°C: Taq polymerase synthesizes complementary strands)
questions.explanation: PCR consists of three successive steps repeated for 30 cycles: (1) Denaturation: The double-stranded DNA template is heated to ~94°C to separate the two strands; (2) Annealing: The reaction temperature is lowered to ~50-60°C (~54°C) to allow two sets of synthetic oligonucleotide primers to anneal to complementary sequences; (3) Extension: Thermostable Taq polymerase extends primers at ~72°C using dNTPs and Mg2+, amplifying the DNA segment billion-fold.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 12 Biology Board Paper 2024 / NCERT Chapter 9 Section 9.2.5

questions.subtopic: Long Answer 1: Human Reproduction (Spermatogenesis Ploidy Stages)
questions.question: Starting from spermatogonia in the human seminiferous tubules, what is the precise chronological sequence of cell types and their ploidy states during spermatogenesis?
options: Spermatogonia (2n) -> Primary spermatocyte (2n) -> Secondary spermatocyte (n) -> Spermatids (n) -> Spermatozoa (n)
Primary spermatocyte (n) -> Secondary spermatocyte (2n) -> Spermatogonia (2n) -> Spermatozoa (n)
Spermatids (2n) -> Secondary spermatocyte (n) -> Primary spermatocyte (2n) -> Spermatozoa (n)
questions.explanation: In human testes, immature male germ cells called spermatogonia (2n = 46) multiply mitotically. Some undergo growth into primary spermatocytes (2n = 46). A primary spermatocyte completes the first meiotic reduction division leading to two equal, haploid cells called secondary spermatocytes (n = 23). These undergo the second meiotic division to produce four equal, haploid spermatids (n = 23), which transform via spermiogenesis into mature spermatozoa (n = 23).
questions.citation: CBSE Class 12 Biology Board Paper 2024 / NCERT Chapter 2 Section 2.2

questions.subtopic: Long Answer 2: Molecular Basis (Lac Operon Gene Functions)
questions.question: In the operon model proposed by Francois Jacob and Jacques Monod, what are the specific catalytic enzymes encoded by the three structural genes lacZ, lacY, and lacA?
options: lacZ encodes beta-galactosidase; lacY encodes permease; lacA encodes transacetylase
lacZ encodes permease; lacY encodes beta-galactosidase; lacA encodes repressor protein
lacZ encodes RNA polymerase; lacY encodes topoisomerase; lacA encodes helicase
lacZ encodes endonuclease; lacY encodes ligase; lacA encodes reverse transcriptase
questions.explanation: The lac operon consists of one regulatory gene (the i gene) and three structural genes (z, y, and a): (1) The z gene codes for beta-galactosidase (beta-gal), primarily responsible for the hydrolysis of the disaccharide lactose into monomeric galactose and glucose; (2) The y gene codes for permease, which increases permeability of the cell to beta-galactosides; and (3) The a gene encodes a transacetylase.

questions.subtopic: Long Answer 3: Biodiversity Conservation (Biodiversity Hotspots Criteria)
questions.question: What two essential biological criteria must a terrestrial geographic region satisfy to be designated as an international Biodiversity Hotspot (Norman Myers)?
options: Exceptional species richness with high degree of endemism (species found nowhere else), and severe degree of threat (loss of at least 70% of its primary habitat)
Presence of at least 10 active volcanic vents and high geothermal microbial diversity
Total absence of human agricultural cultivation and complete geographical isolation on an oceanic island
High density of commercial timber species and commercial medicinal plantations
questions.explanation: Biodiversity hotspots are regions with very high levels of species richness and a high degree of endemism (that is, species confined to that region and not found anywhere else). They are also regions subjected to severe habitat loss (threatened by accelerated human activities). Initially 25 biodiversity hotspots were identified; with subsequent additions, there are now 34 globally, three of which cover India's high biodiversity regions: Western Ghats-Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma, and Himalaya.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 12 Biology Board Paper 2024 / NCERT Chapter 13 Section 13.2.2
